entries.title: Census Housing Vacancies and Homeownership (CPS/HVS)

entries.title: CFPB Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) Data
entries.description: Loan-level data on US mortgage applications, originations and denials reported under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act, published by the CFPB (with the FFIEC) as modified loan/application registers, national snapshot and dynamic datasets, and aggregate reports.

coverage.spatial: United States (loan level; census tract, county, metro, institution)
coverage.temporal: 2017-present on the CFPB data publication site; earlier years on ffiec.gov

entries.attribution: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, HMDA data
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The CFPB page "Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) Data" says "Each year, millions of people apply for mortgages. Using HMDA data, we can learn what happened to the vast majority of those applications". It was last modified Oct. 16, 2026, and links the news item "2025 HMDA Data on Mortgage Lending Now Available" (Mar 31, 2026). The data-publication site https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-publication/ (HTTP 200, redirects to /data-publication/2025) calls HMDA "the most comprehensive publicly available information on mortgage market activity". It offers a weekly-updated "Dynamic National Loan-Level Dataset" and a snapshot dataset ("Data Freeze Date: June 2, 2026"), and says pre-2017 data are at ffiec.gov. The CFPB landing page is cataloged because the data-publication URL redirects to a different year each release.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.consumerfinance.gov/privacy/website-privacy-policy/ states "Information created by the CFPB is in the public domain and you may reproduce, publish, or otherwise use it without the Bureau's permission. Please consider appropriate citation to the Bureau as the source." The released files are compiled from filings by lenders and modified by the CFPB for privacy. The Data Browser API and file formats weren't checked.

The formats, API and bulk download are assumed from other Eurostat entries and weren't checked.

entries.title: FHFA House Price Index
entries.description: The Federal Housing Finance Agency's repeat-sales house price indexes for single-family homes, from national level down to census divisions, states, metro areas, counties, ZIP codes and census tracts, with data back to the mid-1970s.

coverage.spatial: United States (national, census division, state, metro, county, ZIP code, census tract)

entries.attribution: Source: FHFA House Price Index (FHFA HPI®)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page "FHFA House Price Index®" describes "a comprehensive collection of publicly available house price indexes that measure changes in single-family home values based on data that extend back to the mid-1970s from all 50 states and over 400 American cities", using "a weighted, repeat-sales statistical technique". FHFA is an independent federal agency, so its own output is a US Government work. The monthly cadence applies to the headline purchase-only index; other series are quarterly or annual. This wasn't checked per series.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: FHFA's Website Privacy Policy (https://www.fhfa.gov/about/fhfa-policies/website-privacy-policy), section "Copyright and Trademark Notice", states "Generally, information and materials produced by Federal agencies, including FHFA, are in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission". It excludes "marks for which there is a federal trademark as denoted by the ® symbol". "FHFA HPI®" is such a mark, so the name is trademarked though the data are not. The API terms (https://www.fhfa.gov/about/fhfa-policies/api-terms-of-service) bar implying endorsement and modifying content while still attributing it to FHFA. The formats weren't checked.

entries.title: HUD Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) Data
entries.description: Custom tabulations of American Community Survey data that HUD receives from the Census Bureau each year, showing housing problems, cost burden and housing needs by household income, especially for low-income households. Local governments use them to plan how to spend HUD funds in their Consolidated Plans.

coverage.temporal: ACS releases 2006-2008 through 2018-2022, plus older CHAS from the 2000 Census and the 2005-2007 ACS

entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl with a browser User-Agent and headless Chromium; plain curl got HTTP 202, apparently a bot-check response). The page, titled "Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) Data and Tables", says: "Each year, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) receives custom tabulations of American Community Survey (ACS) data from the U.S. Census Bureau. These data, known as the "CHAS" data ..., demonstrate the extent of housing problems and housing needs, particularly for low income households." Latest release: "On December 23, 2025, HUD released updated CHAS data based on 2018-2022 ACS 5-year estimates." The page notes that Census disclosure avoidance has suppressed some estimates since the 2018 tables. It offers a query tool, a data download tool covering "every ACS release from 2006-2008 through 2018-2022", older 2000 and 2005-2007 CHAS as per-state ZIP files, and a CHAS API (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/dataset/chas-api.html) that needs an access token. I did not open the bulk files, so the CSV format is assumed, and I did not read the HUD User API Terms of Service.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: I found no HUD or HUD USER page that states a data licence; the HUD USER disclaimer (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/about/disclaimer.html) has no copyright statement. public-domain is asserted from HUD's status as a federal agency (17 U.S.C. 105), not from a HUD statement. The tabulations are made by the Census Bureau, also a federal agency, for HUD.

entries.title: OECD Affordable Housing Database
entries.description: Cross-country indicators on housing markets, housing conditions and affordability, homelessness and housing exclusion, and public policies towards affordable housing (social rental housing, housing allowances, rental regulation), for OECD countries, Key Partners and EU member states.
entries.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

coverage.spatial: OECD countries, OECD Key Partners and EU member states (national level)
coverage.temporal: varies by indicator ("2024 or latest" for most charts; real house price index 1996-2025)

entries.license: OECD Terms and Conditions, Data section (any purpose including commercial, with credit to the OECD; third-party restrictions may apply)
entries.attribution: OECD (year), OECD Affordable Housing Database, https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/oecd-affordable-housing-database.html (accessed on date)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 in headless Chromium (new headless mode, playwright chromium.launch with channel "chromium") after waiting about 20 seconds, on the second of several attempts; other attempts, curl and a plain client got a Cloudflare "Performing security verification" page (403). The vertical needs reachability.headless: true, and even then the check may be intermittent. The page says the AHD "helps countries monitor access to good-quality affordable housing and strengthen the knowledge base for policy evaluation" and "groups indicators along three dimensions: housing market, housing conditions and affordability, and public policies towards affordable housing". It lists indicators HM1.1-HM1.5, HC1.1-HC4.1 (including HC3.1 "People experiencing homelessness and housing exclusion" and HC3.3 "Evictions") and PH1.1-PH7.1, each with a PDF and most with an XLSX file on webfs.oecd.org/Els-com/Affordable_Housing_Database/. Charts are labelled "2024 or latest" and the real house price index runs 1996-2025. It also links OECD country notes on homelessness and housing exclusion. It complements oecd-house-price-indices. I did not open the XLSX files or check the update cadence.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: OECD Terms & Conditions (https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, read in headless Chromium), section 3 "Data", Permitted Use: "Except where additional restrictions apply as stated above, you can extract from, download, copy, adapt, print, distribute, share and embed Data for any purpose, even for commercial use. You must give appropriate credit to the OECD by using the citation associated with the relevant Data, or, if no specific citation is available, you must cite the source information using the following format: OECD (year), (dataset name),(data source) DOI or URL (accessed on (date))." The section also warns that "Data may be subject to restrictions beyond the scope of these Terms and Conditions" where third parties own them; many AHD indicators are compiled from national sources and EU-SILC, and I did not check per-indicator source notes. These are OECD's own terms, not a named open licence such as CC BY.

Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 in headless Chromium (the Data Explorer is a JavaScript app). The page reads "National and regional house price indices" and says the dataset includes "RPPI compiled by official statistical agencies following international statistical guidelines. It covers all OECD member countries and some non-member countries." It showed "Last updated: October 30, 2026". The SDMX API at sdmx.oecd.org also answered HTTP 200 and lists this dataflow as OECD.SDD.TPS DSD_RHPI@DF_RHPI_ALL, alongside DF_RHPI_TRANSACTIONS (housing transactions) and OECD.ECO.MPD DF_HOUSE_PRICES (analytical house price indicators).

That host returned a Cloudflare "Performing security verification" page (HTTP 403) to curl, headless Chromium and WebFetch, so the Affordable Housing Database was not cataloged. The canonical URL's square brackets are percent-encoded.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: not verified. The Data Explorer footer links its "Terms & conditions" to https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html, which was blocked as above. I did not read OECD's terms, so no licence is asserted. Download formats are taken from the Data Explorer's Download and Developer API buttons and weren't tested.
